subject: Verdant AI pilot kickoff — engagement scaffold & next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Brown <alyssa@verdant.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: pilot goals, scope, and next steps

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the call today. Quick written recap so we have a shared starting point and owners. Please correct anything I mis-stated.

Key pain points you raised:
- Current search/retrieval pipeline is brittle: noisy embeddings + inconsistent reranker scores, frequent hallucination on long-context answers.
- Cost is high at scale; you called out the desire to reduce inference cost per query by ~40%.
- Data residency and access controls are mandatory (PHI-adjacent datasets).

Pilot goals (what success looks like):
1) Precision uplift: +10–15% on top-1 relevance (measured by your eval set).
2) Cost reduction: ~40% reduction in per-query inference cost vs current baseline.
3) Latency: p95 < 150ms for single-turn retrieval+rerank on short queries (able to relax for long generative flows).
4) Production-readiness checklist: S3 access, logging, and basic monitoring validated.

Scope we discussed:
- Ingest ~2M records (sample subset to start).
- Build a retrieval + reranker + concise-generation flow (we will provide prompt templates and candidate rerankers).
- Run a 6-week pilot: provisioned staging infra -> two evaluation checkpoints (week 2 baseline, week 5 final).

Owners / roles (tentative):
- Verdant product: Alyssa Brown (you) — product & prompt approval
- Verdant procurement: Liam O'Connor — contract & SOW
- Redwood AE: Sean Gallagher (me) — program management, cadence
- Redwood Solutions: Dev Patel — infra, onboarding, eval harness
- Redwood CS/SE: Marissa Cole — success criteria & rollout planning

Immediate action items (dates are target):
- Alyssa: confirm data residency requirement (US only) and whether a sample dataset is OK for the first eval — by 2026-12-02.
- Alyssa & Liam: review the attached pilot-charter-v1.pdf and prompt-set-v1.csv, flag any gaps — by 2026-12-03.
- Dev (Redwood): Prep S3/VPC access checklist and a staging API key for tests — by 2026-12-01.
- Liam/Procurement: review SOW draft (attached) and confirm preferred billing/legal terms — target 2026-12-08.

Attachments: pilot-charter-v1.pdf (charter, timeline, success metrics), prompt-set-v1.csv (initial eval prompts), sow-draft-verdant.docx (initial SOW).

Links: HubSpot deal attached in the footer (VDNT-2026-0432). I can start provisioning once we have confirmation on the S3 access pattern and the procurement path is clear.

If this aligns, I suggest we target a formal kickoff (internal provisioning done) the week of 2026-12-06 and a joint kickoff meeting the day we have staging credentials.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189
https://redwood.inference/

From: Alyssa Brown <alyssa@verdant.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@verdant.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pilot goals, scope, and next steps

Thanks, Sean — this is a good summary and close to what we discussed. A couple of clarifications / edits from our side: 

1) Data residency: yes, US-only for now. We will provide a sanitized sample subset for the initial eval. Expect the sample S3 prefix by 2026-12-02.
2) Latency target: we'd be comfortable with p95 < 200ms for the pilot staging environment. If you can achieve 150ms that's great, but please annotate how optimizations change cost.
3) Prompt set: we want ~150 standard prompts and ~50 adversarial prompts focused on hallucination scenarios. Can you expand prompt-set-v1.csv to include the adversarial batch?
4) Procurement: looping Liam in to confirm SOW and timeline expectations. Liam — we prefer a fixed-price pilot with a NDAs already executed; Sean, can you share the DocuSign SOW link and contract points?

We are excited to move. Confirming Verdant will provide: sample dataset (S3 read-only), a list of allowed IPs for allowlist, and an inventory of any third-party PII processors by 2026-12-02.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Brown
Head of Product, Verdant AI
alyssa@verdant.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Brown <alyssa@verdant.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T12:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pilot goals, scope, and next steps

Hi all — quick technical note on provisioning so we can hit the proposed timeline. I'm happy to run a short tech sync (30m) next week to lock details.

What we need from Verdant to get a staging environment up: 
- S3 prefix (or sample tar) with ~10k records for onboarding + a smaller validation set (object keys and path format).
- IAM role or temporary credentials for read-only access to that prefix; least-privilege please.
- IP allowlist CIDRs for VPC egress (if you prefer allowlist rather than VPC peering).
- Preferred VPC peering vs S3 presigned URLs decision. If you want VPC peering, we'll need an AWS account ID and VPC ID.

On our side we'll provide:
- A staging API key (expires after pilot) and an eval harness (python scripts) that will run the baseline and final checkpoints. I'll attach an eval-harness README in the next message.
- A baseline run within 48 hours of receiving access to generate the first set of metrics.

Timing note: if you can share S3 details by 2026-12-02, I can provision the staging env and have a baseline run by 2026-12-04. That keeps us on track for a joint kickoff the week of 2026-12-06.

Small call to action: please reply with the S3 prefix + choice on peering vs presigned URLs and an IP allowlist. If useful, I'm available for a 30m tech call on 2026-12-01 10:00–11:00 PST.

—Dev

Success metrics (final): top-1 relevance +10–15%, cost -~40% vs baseline, staging p95 < 200ms (as requested).
